fields.meta_title: Build an Automated Loan Processing System | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Describe your loan checklist. Emergent builds an automated loan processing system that reads borrower documents and tracks every condition.
fields.h1: Build an Automated Loan Processing System on Your Checklist
fields.hero_description: Build an automated loan processing system that reads borrower documents and sends complete files to underwriting.
fields.features_heading: What a Loan File Needs Before Underwriting
fields.features_subheading: Five of these parts take over steps processors now do by hand. The credit decision stays with your underwriter.
fields.feature_1:
Borrower documents read into fields

Pay stubs, W-2s, and bank statements are read into employer, pay dates, gross pay, and balances as borrowers upload them. A field read with low confidence waits for a processor.
fields.feature_2:
A conditions list on every loan file

Each loan file carries the underwriter's conditions as a checklist. A condition clears when its document arrives and a processor accepts it, and the file shows what is still open.
fields.feature_3:
Upload links and reminders for borrowers

Borrowers get a link that lists only the documents still missing from their file. Reminders go out by email on the schedule you set and stop once the last upload arrives.
fields.feature_4:
Income and debt math, line by line

Income and debt figures are calculated from the documents themselves, and each number links back to its page. Underwriters see the debt-to-income ratio and every input behind it.
fields.feature_5:
Routing by loan type and amount

Complete files land in the right underwriting queue by product and size, with a Slack or email alert. An incomplete application stays with its processor until the last gap is closed.
fields.feature_6:
Your loan app, in your GitHub

The source code exports to your GitHub repository on paid plans. When credit policy adds a field or a second product launches, an engineer edits it there, or you prompt Emergent.

fields.tab_content_1:
Four of five conditions cleared, one chased every 2 days

The Whitford purchase came back from underwriting with five conditions, and four cleared as Lena Whitford uploaded her documents. The gift letter from her father is still open. Until it arrives, she gets an upload link by email every 2 days, and processor Dev Anand sees each reminder on the loan record.
fields.tab_content_2:
Pay stubs in, a ratio out for underwriting

Jonah Albright applies for an $18,000 personal loan and uploads two pay stubs. Each shows $2,750 in gross pay, twice a month, which the app records as $5,500 of gross monthly income. It divides his listed monthly debts of $1,320 by that figure and sends the result to Keisha Ortiz with every input shown.
fields.tab_content_3:
One weak month flagged out of four statements

Harbor Lane Bakery wants a $60,000 equipment loan and uploads four months of business bank statements. The app totals deposits month by month for an average of $34,000. August came in at $12,000, below half the average. That month goes to underwriter Theo Marsh with the statement attached.
fields.tab_content_4:
Funding holds when the contract and approval disagree

Brightwater Auto sends the signed contract for deal 7714. The approval was $24,600, and the contract reads $24,850 after a $250 service plan was added at signing. Funding holds on that deal alone while the dealer is asked for a new contract. Three other deals from the same morning fund on schedule.

fields.howto_title: How to Build Loan Processing Automation
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build an automated loan processing system that collects borrower documents and gives underwriters complete files.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down the checklist you use now
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick one loan product and list every document and check a processor runs before a file reaches underwriting. Include the awkward cases, like a borrower paid in tips or a bank statement with a page missing. That list becomes the first version of the app.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Tell Emergent what a finished loan file holds: borrower details, documents, conditions, and the numbers underwriting reads first. Name the fields a processor must confirm by hand, such as any income figure read from a phone photo of a pay stub.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for a page where borrowers see only the documents their file still needs. Set the reminder schedule, for example an email every three days, and decide which loan officer is copied when a borrower stops replying for a week.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the loan origination system, CRM, or core banking platform your team already works in through its API. Emergent builds the sync: a new application opens a record in the app, and the underwriter's decision is written back to your system of record.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the rules in plain English. Personal loans over $50,000 go to a senior underwriter, and any deposit over $10,000 that is not payroll needs a note from the borrower. The app applies each rule to every file in the same way.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test on files you already closed
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run ten files your team closed last quarter through the app and compare its numbers with what your processors recorded. Fix any field it misreads by prompting Emergent, then run the same ten again until both sets of numbers agree.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go live one product at a time
fields.howto_step_7_des: Switch on one loan product for new applications while older files finish the way they started. After a month of clean files, add the next product, beginning with the one your processors spend the most hours on today.
fields.hero_prompt: Build an automated loan processing system that reads borrower pay stubs and bank statements and tracks the conditions on each file.

faq_plan.q: What does it mean when my loan is processing?
faq_plan.ref: What does it mean when my loan is processing?

prov.original: What does it mean when my loan is processing?

faq_plan.a: It means a loan processor is assembling your file for the underwriter. The processor requests credit reports and gathers documents from you, such as pay stubs and bank statements, then checks them against what you wrote on the application. Answer any request for a missing page quickly, because the file goes to the underwriter only once it is complete.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an automated loan processing system?
faq_plan.a: Describe the checklist your processors follow for one loan product to Emergent's AI automation builder, in plain English. Emergent builds the app from that prompt, with its database, the borrower upload page, and the queue that feeds underwriting. When credit policy changes, you change the app by prompting again. Building and publishing are free to start.

faq_plan.q: What software do loan processors use?
faq_plan.ref: What software do loan processors use?

prov.original: What software do loan processors use?

faq_plan.a: Processors work in a loan origination system, or LOS: a platform used to manage loan applications, which underwriters and closers open too. If your LOS has an API, an app Emergent builds can read each borrower upload into fields and write the figures straight into the matching loan record.

faq_plan.q: What does loan processing automation take off a processor's desk?
faq_plan.a: It takes the typing and the chasing. Pay stub figures land in the file without anyone keying them, and borrowers get reminders without a processor writing each email. The reading step is the one accounts payable automation runs on vendor invoices. A lender that has built either one can reuse the approach for the other.

faq_plan.q: Can mortgage workflow automation track underwriting conditions?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A conditional approval means the lender is likely to approve the loan, but some conditions still need to be met. The app turns each condition into a line with an owner and a due date. Once all of them are met, underwriting reviews what was submitted. Copy the underwriter's own wording into each line, and the borrower's request will match what was asked.

faq_plan.q: Where does borrower data live in a loan automation processing system?
faq_plan.a: It lives in a database you own. Each upload, the figures read from it, and the conditions on the file are stored as records there, not scattered across inboxes. On security, Emergent has SOC 2 Type I and ISO 27001. Have your compliance team review the app before it handles live borrower files.

faq_plan.q: Which borrower documents can an automated loan process read?
faq_plan.a: It can read the documents your processors now key in by hand, including pay stubs, W-2s, tax returns, and bank statements. Each one is read into named fields, such as gross pay on a stub or the closing balance on a statement. Start with the two documents your team types up most, since that is where data entry automation pays back first.

faq_plan.q: Does loan process automation replace loan processors?
faq_plan.a: No. Processors stop keying figures and writing reminder emails, and spend that time calling borrowers about missing pages and writing the note that explains an unusual deposit to the underwriter. The credit decision stays with the underwriter either way. Measure the change in hours per file on one product, not in headcount.

faq_plan.q: What should an automated loan application processing form ask first?
faq_plan.a: Ask first for the answers that set the path of the file: loan product, amount, and purpose. Those answers decide which document list the borrower sees next. A $15,000 personal loan never asks for business bank statements. Emergent can build the application as a conversational flow, one question per screen, which shows a borrower on a phone a single field at a time.

faq_plan.q: What is the final stage of loan processing?
faq_plan.ref: What is the final stage of loan processing?

prov.original: What is the final stage of loan processing?

faq_plan.a: For the processor, it is sending the completed application and every document to the underwriter. The loan itself ends later: origination runs up to disbursal of funds, and on a mortgage, clear to close is the last step ahead of closing day. Before funds go out, match the signed figures against the approval, as you would match a bill in invoice automation.
